prompts.prompt: At the museum entrance, Clara was given a numbered wooden tag for her coat. She put it in her pocket so she could retrieve her coat later.
Alva found a brass thimble beside the workbench and recognized the mark on it. She wrapped it in cloth to return it to the tailor.
A young goat caught its small bell on a fence hook. The farmer brought a soft cloth and walked over to free the goat without hurting it.
Edda borrowed a paintbrush from her class partner before art time. When the bell rang, she looked for her partner to give it back.
The twins carried two lunch boxes with different labels. At the playground, they noticed they had taken the wrong boxes and agreed to trade back.
Mr. Vale saw a new pupil trying to reach a high shelf in the classroom. He offered a small stool and stayed nearby to help.
Nessa made a paper lantern for the evening fair. A dark cloud appeared, so she searched for a covered place to keep the lantern dry.
The gardener lifted a watering can and saw a stream coming from its bottom. He set it down and looked for a way to stop the leak.
Pavel wanted to move a heavy box into the shed, but the cart could not climb the doorstep. He went to fetch a wooden ramp.
Tilda had two blue flags for the village game. She was told to raise the first before breakfast and keep the second folded until after lunch.
The librarian sorted story cards into trays marked yesterday and today. Before opening the new tray, she made sure the old cards were put away.
Hugo shaped three clay bowls on Monday. His teacher said the first bowl had to dry completely before Hugo could paint it on Tuesday.
